tools.title: Decimal Place-Value Builder
tools.description: Build numbers digit by digit in a place-value chart, multiply and divide by 10, and see expanded form, word form and base-ten blocks change.
worksheet: Build 3.47. Write it in expanded form.
Build 3.47 and press × 10. What number do you get?
Start again with 3.47 and press ÷ 10. What number do you get?
In 5.55, the first 5 is worth how many times the second 5?
10 times
Build 0.125. Write it in word form.
one hundred twenty-five thousandths
Which is greater: 0.6 or 0.58? Use the chart to explain.
0.6, because 6 tenths > 5 tenths
Build 2.3 with blocks. How many rods are there?
3 rods (3 tenths)
Reflect: Why do the digits move left when you multiply by 10?
Each place is 10 times the place to its right, so each digit becomes worth 10 times as much.

tools.title: Area Model Explorer
tools.description: Split rectangles into partial products to multiply two-digit numbers, then switch to fractions and multiply parts of a whole.
worksheet: Show 36 × 24. List the four partial products.
What is 36 × 24?
Show 45 × 13. Which partial product is the largest?
Explain why 48 × 25 is not just 40 × 20 + 8 × 5.
That leaves out 40 × 5 and 8 × 20; the full product is 1,200.
Switch to fractions. Show 2/3 × 3/4. What fraction is purple?
How many equal parts is the whole cut into for 2/5 × 1/2?
Reflect: Why is 1/2 × 1/3 smaller than 1/3?
You are taking half of one third, which is less than the whole third.

tools.title: Expression Builder
tools.description: Type or tap to build numerical expressions with parentheses, brackets and braces, then watch them evaluated one step at a time.
worksheet: Evaluate 4 + 3 × 2. What is done first?
3 × 2 first; the answer is 10.
Evaluate (4 + 3) × 2.
Evaluate 2 × [5 + (6 − 2)]. List the steps.
Put parentheses in 3 + 5 × 2 to make it equal 16.
Write an expression for: add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2.
How does 3 × (125 + 48) compare with 125 + 48?
3 times as large
Reflect: Why do we need grouping symbols?
They show which part to do first, so everyone gets the same answer.

tools.title: Fraction Explorer
tools.description: Build two fractions with fraction bars, find equivalent fractions and a common denominator, and compare, add or subtract them.
worksheet: Show 1/2 and 1/3. What is the least common denominator?
Which is greater: 3/5 or 5/8?
Find two different fractions that are equivalent to 2/3.
Find 2/3 + 3/4. Write the answer as a mixed number.
Explain why 1/2 + 1/3 is not 2/5.
2/5 is less than 1/2, but adding 1/3 must make the sum bigger than 1/2.
Reflect: Why do we need a common denominator?
So that we are adding parts of the same size.

tools.title: Measurement Converter
tools.description: Convert customary and metric measurements, see the conversion fact as a picture, and decide when to multiply or divide.
worksheet: Convert 3 ft to inches.
36 in
Convert 50 in to feet and inches.
4 ft 2 in
How many cups are in 1 gallon?
16 cups
Convert 2.5 kg to grams.
Convert 350 cm to meters.
Convert 3 lb 4 oz to ounces.
52 oz
When do you multiply to convert? When do you divide?
Multiply going to a smaller unit; divide going to a bigger unit.
Reflect: Why does the number get bigger when you change feet to inches?
Inches are smaller, so it takes more of them to make the same length.

tools.title: Volume Builder
tools.description: Stack unit cubes into rectangular prisms, see layers and base area, and connect counting cubes to V = l × w × h and composite figures.
worksheet: Build 4 × 3 × 2. How many cubes are in the bottom layer?
What is the volume of 4 × 3 × 2?
24 cubic units
Find two different prisms with volume 36.
Examples: 6 × 3 × 2, 4 × 3 × 3
A prism has base area 15 and height 4. What is its volume?
60 cubic units
Build a composite figure: Prism A 3 × 2 × 4 and Prism B 2 × 2 × 2. Total volume?
32 cubic units
Why do we use cubic units for volume?
Volume counts cubes that fill space in three directions.
If you double the height, what happens to the volume?
It doubles.
Reflect: Explain why l × w × h counts every cube, even hidden ones.
l × w counts one full layer, and h counts how many layers are stacked.

tools.title: Coordinate Plane Explorer
tools.description: Plot points in the first quadrant by clicking or typing, connect them into shapes, measure distances along grid lines, and graph two-rule patterns.
worksheet: Plot (2, 7). Describe how you moved from the origin.
2 units right, then 7 units up
Plot (7, 2). Is it the same point as (2, 7)?
No
Plot (1, 4) and (8, 4). How far apart are they?
7 units
Plot three corners of a rectangle: (2, 1), (6, 1), (6, 5). Where is the fourth corner?
What is the perimeter of that rectangle?
16 units
Make pattern points with x adds 2 and y adds 4. List the first three points.
In those pattern points, how does y compare with x?
y is 2 times x
Reflect: Why does the order of the numbers in an ordered pair matter?
The first number is the move right and the second is the move up; switching them gives a different point.
